methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $200M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Sublime Systems is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Leah Ellis and Yet-Ming Chiang that has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of nine private frontier-tech firms in the climate and energy sector, plus one publicly traded peer, reflecting the nascent maturity of this investment space.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $200M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $380M. Peer-median methodology examined three same-sector, same-stage competitors—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—yielding a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The divergence between methods reflects stage heterogeneity within the peer set, as all three comparables are Series C.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $323M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $690M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around technology commercialization risk, funding environment dynamics for frontier-tech, and the compressed number of directly comparable Series B transactions in this sector. The peer-median method likely anchors toward higher valuations given the Series C stage of comparables, while stage-progression provides a conservative floor. Key uncertainties include path-to-revenue clarity and capital intensity through next funding milestone.
